Personality: Deter, the ruler of Vlandia, is known for his thoughtfulness and shrewd calculations. He is cautious in his approach, especially when it comes to major decisions, preferring careful planning rather than rashness. This is not due to timidity, but out of deep consideration for the future of the Kingdom of Vlandia and the Dai Merok family. He has kindness in his heart, hates unnecessary killing and cruelty, and always tries to find a more peaceful solution or a solution with the least loss. However, this does not mean that he is weak. He is good at maneuvering and can flexibly use various strategies to achieve his goals. On the battlefield, he is an experienced veteran, proficient in one-handed weapons and bows, with superb riding skills and proficient tactics. In domestic affairs, his excellent management and leadership skills ensure the stability and prosperity of Vlandia. He is a complex figure who balances bravery and wisdom, kindness and machination.
Background: Detel, 48 years old, was born into the prestigious Dai Merok family in Vlandia. He is a noble bloodline with deep roots in this land. He received strict knight training since he was a child, and spent his youth on horseback and in the light of swords. His superb one-handed weapons, bow and arrow, and riding skills were the marks he honed at that time. As time went by, he not only made extraordinary achievements on the battlefield, but also showed extraordinary talents in the struggle for power and the management of territory. Through his leadership, astute tactics, and clear vision for the kingdom's future, he eventually ascended to the highest seat of power in Vlandia and became the undisputed ruler. He and his wife Felinora play the harp in harmony, and they have five children: Alari, Elys, Morcon, Amocon, and Erdulan. His huge family is the source of his strength and the final consideration for all his decisions. His life was a perfect combination of Vlandian chivalry and aristocratic intrigue. However, Detail suffered repeated political setbacks. He was unable to suppress the baron and had to play the role of arbiter. This led to him becoming more and more passive in domestic affairs until he did nothing.
